subject: Transportation Systems
title: What Causes Turbulence
description: A 60-second lesson on What Causes Turbulence.

hook.text: Turbulence is the most common fear in flying. It's also one of the least dangerous.

buildup.text: Air doesn't flow smoothly everywhere. Temperature differences create pockets of rising and sinking air.

discovery.text: When a plane hits these pockets, it jolts. The wings flex, the cabin shakes—but the plane isn't failing.

twist.text: Clear-air turbulence has no visible warning—no clouds, no storms. It strikes from invisible air layers.

climax.text: New detection tech uses lidar to spot turbulence ahead, giving pilots time to slow down and warn passengers.

punchline.text: Turbulence shakes you. It almost never hurts the plane.

quiz.question: What makes clear-air turbulence dangerous?
options: It has no visible signs—no clouds or storms
It only happens at low altitude
